payload.title: guards' judge is dark
payload.body: Root cause, diagnosed: a latch in the omp session extension (forge's omp adapter, render.ts, projected to ~/.omp/agent/extensions/cratylus-session.ts). The in-process judge (the advisor role, anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 on this host) has a 22 s deadline per call; after three consecutive timeouts, askJudge returns no verdict WITHOUT calling the judge again, and the miss count is reset only by an answer. Since a latched judge is never asked, it can never answer: one transient burst of slow calls (loop-ledger fanned out implementers and assayers against the same provider) blacked out all three omp guards for the rest of the session. The judge model itself is healthy: a direct call answered in 5 s. Not configuration. The enforcement scope concept already requires every firing to be judged where the judge can run, so this is a realization defect: the latch must expire, retrying the judge after a cooldown. Also: dark notices dedupe per distinct line, so three guards alternating defeat the dedupe. and the host's own `judge` model role is not read by the extension (it reads advisor, smol, tiny). Immediate relief: a new session resets the latch. After reinstalling 0.7.0 another omp session judged a turn (a BLOCK) and then went dark once, so the judge answers again but still times out at times; this session's own turn end left no verdict record, which is unexplained. The host's `judge` model role is omp's own (Jev, for search relevance) and unrelated to the guards, which judge on the advisor role.
